acceptance: compare gains a documented option for a minimum absolute regression delta, with unit tests for a query that exceeds both limits, one that exceeds only the percentage, and one that exceeds only the delta
The nightly-v2 perf step uses the option, and the chosen floor is justified from the per-query spread in retained t3-perf-result artifacts
A real regression (a large slowdown on a long-running query) still fails the gate in a test
docs for the perf gate describe the floor
context: Failing queries differ from night to night (2026-10-05 failed on a different set than 2026-10-08), which points to noise rather than a stable slowdown. Checked at plan time: `uv run benchbox compare --help` lists only --fail-on-regression for this purpose.
description: The nightly T3 perf gate fails on per-query percentage change alone. In run 37794806634 (2026-10-08) total time improved 20.35% and 19 of 22 queries got faster, but Q8 (9.0 to 11.6 ms, +28.9%) and Q20 (10.0 to 11.9 ms, +19.0%) failed the 10% threshold on a 2 to 3 ms change. `benchbox compare` has no option for a minimum absolute delta, so the gate cannot tell scheduling jitter from a regression at this scale. Raising the threshold to 20% is not enough: Q8 would still fail at +28.9%. Add a minimum absolute delta (for example `--min-regression-delta 5ms`) that a query must exceed, in addition to the percentage, before it counts as a regression, then use it in the nightly-v2 perf step. Choose the floor from retained runs rather than by guess.
